items.q: What's the highest-leverage move with $0 of your own money?
items.a: Convince a parent to open a **custodial investing account** at **age 13**. **Time in the market** beats timing; UK **Junior ISA** (£9,000/year) or US **UGMA/UTMA**, defaulting to a low-cost **S&P 500** index fund.

items.q: What does "stash, don't save" mean at 15?
items.a: Ask for **cash** instead of depreciating gifts, get a Saturday job, and treat money as a **launch pad** — not a theme-park fund. Even **$100 beats $0** for seeding the next income step.

items.q: How should a 16-year-old invest limited cash?
items.a: Buy **equipment**, not fake guru courses. Mark's son put **$500 into an iMac** for video editing/Photoshop; **community learning** beats solo courses so you arrive at 18 with value to sell.

items.q: Why is a driving license a money tool, not just convenience?
items.a: Not driving **blocks side hustles** (clients 30 min away, bad transit). Pass early, use stash for a **cheap starter car**, and treat timing as: **early = on time, on time = late**.

items.q: What banking and credit setup does Mark want at 18?
items.a: **Dual accounts**: checking for cash flow + high-interest savings for a **3–6 month emergency fund** (separate banks). Get a **credit card**, pay in full monthly — credit score is the **"Uber rating for money."**

items.q: Why do tax wrappers and early compounding matter so much?
items.a: Use **Roth IRA / ISA / TFSA** (etc.) — contribution limits prove they are powerful. **$250/month from 18 → ~$1.5M** vs **~$679K starting at 28**; ~**10 extra years ≈ 2×** outcome at the same contribution.

items.q: Is university always the wealth path?
items.a: ROI is **career-specific**. Consider **apprenticeships** as paid alternatives; **$60–100K debt** is a trap for degrees that aren't required (e.g. golf management).

items.q: What debt should teens and new adults avoid?
items.a: Avoid **consumer/bad debt** — if you can't buy a non-wealth-creating thing outright, don't finance it. Mark flags **2.2M UK drivers** on car finance as a silent wealth killer.
